expect:
A digital counting system uses a 4017 decade counter clocked at 20 Hz. Q5 is connected to the MR pin. The ten Q outputs are each connected to an LED.
(a) State how many LEDs will light in sequence before the counter resets. [1 mark]
(b) Calculate the flash rate of each LED. [2 marks]
(c) A student claims that after the counter resets at Q5, the Q5 LED stays lit for one full clock cycle. Evaluate this claim. [3 marks]
(d) Explain the purpose of the decoder/driver IC when a 4017 counter drives a 7-segment display. [2 marks]
value:
A digital counting system uses a 4017 decade counter clocked at 20 Hz. Q5 is connected to the MR pin. The ten Q outputs are each connected to an LED.
(a) State how many LEDs will light in sequence before the counter resets. [1 mark]
(b) Calculate the flash rate of each LED. [2 marks]

find: Any noise signal whose amplitude is smaller than the hysteresis band cannot cause a false triggering event.
replace: Noise that does not carry the input across the next switching threshold cannot change the output.
note: F8: Whether one noise pulse switches the output depends on the starting voltage.

find: Any noise spike smaller than 2.0 V cannot cause a false output transition — the output stays rock steady until the input genuinely crosses a threshold.
replace: A noise spike changes the output only if it carries the input across the relevant switching threshold.
note: F8: State the threshold condition rather than an unconditional amplitude rule.

expect:
A Schmitt inverter is connected to a sensor. The input voltage rises slowly from 0 V. The output switches from HIGH to LOW when the input reaches 3.2 V. The input then falls; the output switches back to HIGH when the input reaches 1.6 V.
(a) State the upper threshold voltage Vᵀ₊. [1 mark]
(b) Calculate the hysteresis voltage. [1 mark]
(c) A noise spike of amplitude 1.0 V is present on the input. State whether this spike will cause a false output transition. Justify your answer. [2 marks]
value:
A Schmitt inverter is connected to a sensor. The input voltage rises slowly from 0 V. The output switches from HIGH to LOW when the input reaches 3.2 V. The input then falls; the output switches back to HIGH when the input reaches 1.6 V.
(a) State the upper threshold voltage Vᵀ₊. [1 mark]
(b) Calculate the hysteresis voltage. [1 mark]
(c) The input is otherwise at 0 V. A noise spike takes it to 1.0 V. State whether this spike will cause a false output transition. Justify your answer. [2 marks]
note: F8: Supply the starting voltage needed to determine the result.

expect:
(a) Vᵀ₊ = 3.2 V [1 mark]
(b) Hysteresis = 3.2 − 1.6 = 1.6 V [1 mark]
(c) No, the spike will not cause a false transition [1 mark]; because the spike amplitude (1.0 V) is smaller than the hysteresis band (1.6 V), so the input cannot cross both thresholds [1 mark].
value:
(a) Vᵀ₊ = 3.2 V [1 mark]
(b) Hysteresis = 3.2 − 1.6 = 1.6 V [1 mark]
(c) No, the spike will not cause a false transition [1 mark]; because the input reaches only 1.0 V, below the 3.2 V upper threshold [1 mark].
note: F8: Mark the answer against the stated threshold, not hysteresis amplitude alone.

expect: The difference between the upper and lower switching thresholds of a Schmitt trigger, giving it immunity to noise signals smaller than this band.
value: The difference between the upper and lower switching thresholds of a Schmitt trigger, helping prevent repeated switching caused by noise near a threshold.
note: F8: Hysteresis does not make every smaller noise pulse incapable of one transition.
